q6.answer: The status lives in the export record (row in the new report_exports table on the primary database), with status queued, running, done or failed. The page loads GET /api/reports/{id}/exports/latest on load, including when the user returns later, and after a 202 reply. While the status is queued or running it polls every 5 seconds, and it stops on done or failed.

q7.answer: The job streams the report. It reads the read replica in keyset pages of 5,000 rows, writes CSV into one 8 MB in-memory buffer, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part, keeping only the etags. Memory stays at about one buffer plus one page plus the etag list. About 113 parts for 900 MB is far below the 10,000 limit.

q8.answer: Uploaded parts are invisible until complete_multipart succeeds, so nothing partial is downloadable. If the handler can still run, it aborts the upload, sets the row back to queued and re-raises. If the worker dies, the row stays running with its old upload_id, and the next attempt aborts that upload. The bucket also discards uploads left over after 24 hours. The next attempt restarts from the first row and a new upload, because no progress is saved. Resuming is deliberately left out, as an open question.

q9.answer: At the click, the validated filters and cols are saved as text on the report_exports record, which is the only place they are kept. The queue payload carries only the export_id. The job loads the record and reads the view from it, so the job uses the view as it was at the click.

q10.answer: A unique partial index on (user_id, report_id) where status IN ('queued','running'), in the database. The insert uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING. If it returns no row, the request lost the race and selects the active export and returns it with existing true. So two simultaneous clicks make one record and one job.

q11.answer: The file must be complete (complete_multipart returned), and the record must be marked done with expires_at set in one update where status is running. Then signed_url is made for the time left until expires_at, and the email is sent, and notified_at is set. If the queue runs the job again and the record is done, the handler skips the upload and goes straight to the email step, which sends only if notified_at is empty. If notified_at is set, it returns and sends nothing. If it is failed, it returns without raising.

q12.answer: Nothing is stored and no job exists. Any error before the last row returns a 500 with no file, because the CSV is built fully in memory and sent only when complete. So a cut-off file never looks whole, and the user can click again. There is no retry and no failure email.
